newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Few prices rise, others weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Few prices rise, others weak.

text.p: Cash millfeed prices rose at a few locations in reaction to some fill-in buying, while prices were unchanged to lower at other locations, millfeed dealers said.

All dealers said feedmixers and livestock producers appear to be well-supplied with feed through spring, and those who need feed can choose from adequate supplies of millfeeds, soymeal, corn and sorghum.

"The only thing that is not tight right now is hay," said a Kansas dealer. He said extremely heavy snowfall in the Dakotas this winter, has ranchers there buying hay from Nebraska, Kansas and Oklahoma.
"I think there is going to be plenty of millfeeds," said a Minnesota dealer. "The (mill) run times tend to be increasing."
Dealers said demand for millfeeds was often subdued in late January and early February but hopeed that buying interest would pick up later in the month.
Also, with corn prices sharply lower from the record high levels last summer, farmers stored much of their corn to feed to their hogs, dealers said.
